Character Creation

Arneyan Campaign Setting

A quick-reference overview of how a character comes together in Arneyan, with a short summary of each section below. Full detail for each section is given in its own part of this document. Classes are covered in Book III: Classes and aren't repeated here.

Follow these steps in order. Each one points to the section that covers it in full.

Step 1: Choose an ancestry. Note its size, speed, traits, languages and its fixed attribute bonus and penalty (see Ancestries, below). Choose a subtype if your ancestry has one.

Step 2: Choose a class and Kit. Read the class's chapter in Classes. You gain its 1st-level features and your Kit (or Path) abilities straight away.

Step 3: Generate attributes. Use Method V, assign the six scores, then apply your ancestry bonus and penalty and look up each modifier on the Arneyan Modifier Table. No attribute can start above 18 (see Starting Scores).

Step 4: Roll Starting Luck. Roll 4d6, drop the lowest die and add the rest. This is both your Starting Luck and your Current Luck.

Step 5: Work out hit points. At 1st level, Max HP is the maximum of your class Hit Die plus your Constitution modifier (minimum 1). From 2nd level you roll the die and add your Constitution modifier each level, or take the average. From 11th level you gain a flat amount instead, a third of your Hit Die rounded down (d4 +1, d6 +2, d8 +2, d10 +3, d12 +4), plus your Constitution modifier (minimum 1 HP a level). Each class lists its amount.

Step 6: Choose skills and languages. You start Trained in 3 different skills (NWP), and can learn more in downtime. You know your ancestry's languages plus one more for each point of Intelligence modifier, plus any your ancestry lets you choose.

Step 7: Choose a Feat. Every class gains one at 1st level. Choose from the General Path and the path or paths open to your class.

Step 8: Choose spells, if you cast. Casters choose their cantrips and spells using their class chapter and Spellcasting in Arneyan.

Step 9: Buy equipment. Roll your class's starting money and spend it from the Shopkeeper's Catalogue. Your carrying capacity is 18 slots (20 at Strength 13 to 15, 22 at 16 or more, 16 at 6 or less).

Step 10: Choose an alignment and a Background Story. Pick an Outlook and one or two tenets (see Alignment in Arneyan) and write a few lines on where your character comes from. The Background Story Bonus can later grant Advantage when it applies.

Step 11: Fill in the numbers. AC = 10 + armour bonus + Dexterity modifier (limited by armour category) + shield + any Feat or class bonuses. Attack roll = d20 + attribute modifier + BtH. Saving throw = d20 + attribute modifier + the greater of 1 and half your level (Fortitude uses Constitution, Reflex uses Dexterity, Will uses Wisdom). Initiative = d20 + Dexterity modifier. Speed comes from your ancestry.

Worked Example: Brenna, Dwarf Fighter

Ancestry: Dwarf: Medium, speed 25ft, darkvision 60ft, +2 Constitution, +1 Wisdom, −1 Charisma.

Class and Kit: Fighter (d10 Hit Die, BtH +0) with the Gladiator Kit. At 1st level she has Weapon Specialisation, Combat Manoeuvres and Combat Reflexes, plus the Kit's Crowd's Favourite and Arena Presence.

Attributes: Method V Set Alpha gives 17, 15, 14, 12, 11, 9. Brenna assigns Strength 17, Constitution 15, Dexterity 14, Wisdom 12, Intelligence 11, Charisma 9. The Dwarf bonuses make Constitution 17, Wisdom 13 and Charisma 8. Her Feat (below) raises Constitution to 18. Modifiers: Strength +2, Dexterity +1, Constitution +3, Intelligence +0, Wisdom +1, Charisma −1.

Luck: She rolls 4d6 and gets 5, 4, 3, 2. Dropping the 2 gives a Starting Luck of 12.

Hit points: Maximum of the d10 (10) plus Constitution modifier +3 = 13, plus 1 from Toughness = 14 Max HP.

Skills and languages: Trained in Heraldry, Cooking and Engineering, plus Armourer as the Dwarf's free Craft skill. Intelligence +0 gives no bonus language, so she knows only her ancestry languages.

Feat: Toughness (+1 Max HP per level, +1 Constitution, Advantage on Constitution checks).

Equipment: She rolls 3d6 for starting money (4, 5, 3 = 12), so 12 gp. She buys a Chain Mail Shirt (10 gp), a Medium Wooden Shield (5 sp), a Spear (1 sp) and a Backpack (2 sp): 10 gp 8 sp, with 1 gp 2 sp left. These take 4 of her 20 slots, since the Backpack takes none.

AC: 10 + 4 (Chain Mail Shirt) + 1 (Dexterity; Medium armour allows up to +2) + 1 (shield) = 16.

Attack: With her Spear, d20 + 2 (Strength) + 0 (BtH) + 1 (Weapon Specialisation, Hook) = +3, and +1 damage.

Saves: Fortitude +4 (Constitution +3, plus 1), Reflex +2 (Dexterity +1, plus 1), Will +2 (Wisdom +1, plus 1).

• Size & Traits: sets your size, speed, darkvision, a fixed attribute bonus and penalty, and a handful of innate traits
  • Humanoids: a lore catch-all for generic NPCs only — not a selectable option at character creation

See Arneyan Ancestries — Stats & Mechanics Reference for every ancestry's complete stat block, traits, and attribute modifiers.

• Method V: roll two sets of six descending dice pools (8d6 down to 3d6), then choose one set to keep
  • Safety Nets: the Donation Rule and the Gygaxian Threshold stop anyone ending up with an unplayable character
  • Quick Roll (optional): 4d6, dropping the lowest, six times, with the same threshold and cap
  • Starting Scores: no score starts above 18; ancestry or creation-feat points that would go over move to another attribute
  • Modifiers: attribute modifiers follow Arneyan's compressed scale

See Attributes and Method V for the complete rolling procedure and table rules.

• What It Is: a seventh, fluctuating stat separate from your six attributes — fate's favour and your character's raw survival instinct
  • Starting Score: roll 4d6 drop lowest
  • Burn: +1 per point spent on a d20 roll (attack, save or check; never damage)
  • Luck Checks: roll d20 equal to or under your Luck when fate itself is in question (the only roll-under mechanic)
  • Last Chance: once each time they are dying, a dying character may burn 1 Luck to make an immediate stabilisation roll (Fortitude save, DC 10); success stops the dying but leaves them unconscious
  • Recovery: +1 on levelling up, plus GM rewards (including +1 for acting on a tenet) — never from rest alone; Luck can never exceed 20

See The Luck Stat for the complete mechanic and the GM's guidance on running it at the table.

• Progression: characters gain Feats at set levels based on their class group: training, cosmic favour, or survival instinct earned through experience
  • Path Tables: drawn from General, Martial, Specialist, or Arcane & Devout, restricted by class
  • Hybrids: can choose from either of their two thematic Paths

See The Feats of Arneyan for the complete Feat Progression table, Path restrictions, and every available Feat.

• What They Are: background, utility, and lore skills that expand what a character can do outside combat
  • Learning: every character starts Trained in 3 different skills; more are learned in downtime, with no limit and no link to level
  • Access: no class restriction on which proficiencies a character can take

See Skills (NWP) for the training-tier rules and the complete Master Proficiency List.

• Common: universal across Veradyna — every people and nation speaks it without exception
  • Ancestry Languages: every ancestry grants one or more languages tied to its heritage, for free
  • Bonus Languages: every character also knows additional languages equal to their Intelligence modifier (minimum 0)
  • Choosing: freely from the Common Tongues (e.g. Dwarvish, Elvish) or, where a class feature, Kit, Patron, or NWP grants access, the rarer Rare Tongues (e.g. Draconic, Infernal, Thieves' Cant)
  • Stacking: ancestry languages sit on top of the Intelligence-modifier pool — they never compete with it
  • Literacy: assumed in any language you know, unless your background says otherwise (GM discretion)
  • NWPs: the Languages, Ancient and Languages, Modern Skills grant additional languages beyond this starting allotment

See Languages of Veradyna for the complete Ancestry Language table and every Common and Rare Tongue.

Alignment in Arneyan

Arneyan Campaign Setting

In Arneyan, mortals are not truly good or evil. Gods, fiends, celestials and the undead are: they are the powers of a real war between Law and Chaos, Good and Evil. Mortals live in the middle of that war. Their societies lean towards the powers that shape them, but each mortal is free to choose, and most never take a side.

• Starting Money: roll based on your class category (5d4 sp for a Monk up to 3d6 gp for the wealthiest martial and divine classes)
  • Shopping: spend it using the Shopkeeper's Catalogue
  • Carrying Capacity: a Strength-scaled inventory grid (18 slots baseline, 20 at Strength 13 to 15, 22 at 16+, 16 at 6 or less) rather than weight
  • Quick Start: a curated Basic Necessities list, common starting weapons, and six pre-built Starting Packs

See Starting Equipment & Gear for all of it, plus where to find full pricing on everything else.

Multiclassing

Arneyan Campaign Setting

The Basics

When: multiclassing is chosen at character creation, not added later, unless the GM approves a reason in the story (training under a mentor, a life-changing event and the like).

Combinations: any ancestry may combine any number of classes, three or more included.

Attribute requirement: a score of 13 or more in each combined class's key attribute.

Arneyan Ancestries

Stats & Mechanics Reference

A mechanics-first reference. Every ancestry below lists its size, speed, darkvision, and attribute bonus/penalty in a single summary line, followed by its complete set of innate traits.

Sub-type entries add to the ancestry's base traits rather than replacing them, and use identical stats to their parent ancestry unless noted otherwise. A sub-type never has its own attribute bonuses; choose it for its traits. The exceptions are Genasi castes and Shifter lineages, which carry their own attribute bonus.

Weapon and armour training from an ancestry adds those weapons to your class's list and removes the penalties for wearing that armour. It never lets a class that lists "None" for armour cast in it.

Where an ancestry trait forces a saving throw without stating a DC, the DC is 10 + half your level (minimum 1) + the modifier of the stated attribute (Level is character level). Unless a trait says otherwise, this uses Constitution for breath, poison and bite effects and Strength for grapple, knockdown and shove effects. This is the Ancestry Save DC.

Aasimar

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Wis / +1 Cha, −1 Str

Traits

  • Resistance 5 to necrotic & radiant. At will: bright light 10ft radius (illumination only).
  • Celestial Wings (1st): wings of light let you glide. You take no damage from falls, and move 2ft sideways for every 1ft you drop. From 3rd level your wings carry you: you have a fly speed equal to your walking speed.
  • Ascension (5th): once per day, your fly speed doubles for the encounter (1 Luck for a second use).
  • Flight: you can't fly in medium or heavy armour or while over your carrying limit; from 9th level you can fly in any armour you are trained in (still not over your carrying limit). You fall if you are knocked Prone, Stunned, Paralysed or Unconscious in the air (see Falling Damage in The Arneyan Codex).
  • Advantage on saves vs frightened.
  • Choose one Wisdom or Charisma skill at creation; you have Advantage on checks with it. This is not a Proficiency tier and is not one of your 3 starting skills.

Automaton

Size Small / Medium / Large (chosen at creation) • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Con / +1 Int, −1 Cha

Traits

  • Immune to effects targeting biological creatures, including poison and disease (still healed by magic, still affected mentally); doesn't need to breathe or sleep, though a long rest is still required (low-power idle).
  • Advantage on Strength checks to force/break/overpower.
  • Choose one Craft or Engineering skill at creation; you have Advantage on checks with it. This is not a Proficiency tier and is not one of your 3 starting skills.

Subtypes

  • 1st Generation: +1 natural armour AC, Advantage on saves vs forced shutdown/disable/override.
  • 2nd Generation and later: Choose one additional Craft, Engineering or precision skill; you have Advantage on checks with it (two chosen skills in total), plus Modular Repair (field maintenance, once per day; restore 1d8 + Constitution modifier HP; 1 Luck for a second use).

Bugbear

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Str / +1 Dex, −1 Int

Traits

  • +5ft reach on melee attacks.
  • Once per encounter, bonus damage = character level vs a creature that hasn't acted yet (1 Luck for a second trigger per encounter).
  • Advantage on Stealth checks despite size.
  • Weapon training: morningstar, javelin, light crossbow, greatclub.
  • Armour training: light, medium.

Changeling

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Cha / +1 Dex, −1 Wis

Traits

  • Shapechanger: alter appearance to any similar-size humanoid as an action (clothing/gear unaffected).
  • Advantage on checks to imitate a specific voice/mannerism once observed.
  • Advantage on saves vs charmed.
  • Advantage on Insight checks to detect deception aimed at them.
  • Perfect Mask: Once per day, your assumed disguise becomes undetectable for one scene, resisting even magical discernment (1 Luck for a second use).

Deep Gnomes (Svirfneblin)

Size Small • Speed 25ft • Darkvision 120ft • +2 Int / +1 Wis, −1 Cha

Traits

  • Advantage on Stealth in stone/rocky terrain.
  • Innate Nondetection: always on, you can't be found by divination magic.
  • Innate Blindness/Deafness: 1/day (Fortitude save, Ancestry Save DC, Constitution).
  • Advantage on Will saves vs magic.
  • Weapon training: dagger, light hammer, heavy pick, hand crossbow.

Dragonborn

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Str / +1 Cha, −1 Dex

Traits

  • Draconic type: choose fire, cold, lightning, poison or acid at creation. Once per day breath weapon of that type: line or cone, damage = character level, Reflex save for half (Ancestry Save DC, Constitution; 1 Luck for an extra use).
  • Resistance 5 to your draconic type.
  • Advantage on Charisma checks towards other dragon-kin and true dragons.
  • Weapon training: longsword, spear, greatclub, javelin.

Duergar

Size Medium • Speed 25ft (not reduced by armour or encumbrance) • Darkvision 120ft • +2 Con / +1 Wis, −1 Cha

Traits

  • Disadvantage on attack rolls and sight-based Perception checks in direct sunlight.
  • Advantage on saves vs illusion, charm, and paralysis.
  • Advantage on stonework/underground construction/unusual-stonework checks.
  • Innate Invisibility, 1/day, until you attack or cast, or up to 1 minute (1 Luck for a second use, or to cast Enlarge instead).
  • Weapon training: warhammer, handaxe, light crossbow, heavy pick.
  • Armour training: light, medium.

Dwarf

Size Medium • Speed 25ft (not reduced by armour or encumbrance) • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Con / +1 Wis, −1 Cha

Traits

  • Advantage on stonework/underground construction/unusual-stonework checks.
  • Advantage on saves vs poison; Resistance 5 to poison damage.
  • Choose one Craft skill at creation; you have Advantage on checks with it. This is not a Proficiency tier and is not one of your 3 starting skills.
  • The Clan Weapon (Disadvantage on Charisma checks with other dwarves if lost, until recovered).
  • Stonebraced: Once per day, treat an incoming critical hit as a normal hit, or ignore a knockdown.
  • Weapon training: handaxe, battleaxe, warhammer, light crossbow, firearms.
  • Armour training: light, medium.

Subtypes

  • Dul Khagul: Advantage identifying clan lineage/weapon origin/traditions; Advantage on saves vs being charmed or persuaded against clan loyalty.
  • Tenor Hold: Advantage on craft/repair/identify firearms & mechanical devices; Advantage on checks involving human cultures and languages.

Elf

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Low-Light Vision (not true darkvision) • +2 Dex / +1 Int, −1 Con

Traits

  • Immune to magical sleep.
  • Advantage on saves vs charm.
  • Trance (4hr rest instead of 8hr sleep).
  • Keen Senses: Advantage on Perception checks (sight or hearing) and on concentration saves to maintain spells.
  • Armour training: light.

Subtypes

  • High Elf: weapon training (longsword/shortsword/longbow/rapier), one Wizard cantrip at creation, Arcane Sense (innately sense the presence and rough direction of significant magical auras or arcane sites, such as wards, ley-adjacent places and active enchantments, within 60ft, with no check).
  • Saevren (Wood Elf): weapon training (longbow/shortbow/shortsword/handaxe), +5ft speed, Advantage on Stealth/Perception in natural environments, Camouflage (once per day, as part of your movement while in natural terrain: become undetectable to passive notice until you move or act).
  • Iiria Elf (Jinia coastal): weapon training (shortsword/longbow/spear/net), Advantage on checks/saves involving navigation/sailing/coastal environments, Advantage on Perception at sea or on coastlines, Sea Legs (once per day: reroll a failed Reflex save while aboard a vessel or in open water).

Firbolg

Size Large • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Str / +1 Wis, −1 Cha

Traits

  • Hardy (Advantage on Fortitude saves against disease and harsh weather).
  • Powerful Build (Advantage on Strength checks to push, drag or lift).
  • Speech of Beast and Leaf (simple communication with beasts/plants). Once per day: invisible as part of your movement until you attack or cast, or until the end of your next turn (1 Luck for extra use).
  • Advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to live off the land or avoid detection travelling.
  • Weapon training: club, staff, spear, sling.

Genasi

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • Constitution + caste attribute (see below)

  • Fire: +2 Con / +1 Cha, −1 Wis
  • Earth: +2 Con / +1 Str, −1 Cha
  • Water: +2 Con / +1 Wis, −1 Dex
  • Air: +2 Con / +1 Dex, −1 Str

Traits

  • Resistance 5 to a damage type by caste.
  • Doesn't need to breathe; can hold breath indefinitely.
  • One Sorcerer cantrip themed to caste at creation.
  • Castes: Fire: Charisma-themed, resist fire, Advantage on illusion/storytelling checks.
  • Earth: Strength-themed, resist poison, Advantage on stonework/mountainous-terrain checks.
  • Water: Wisdom-themed, resist cold, Advantage on swimming/sailing/open-water checks.
  • Air: Dexterity-themed, resist lightning, Advantage on balance/falling/sudden-movement checks.

Gnome

Size Small • Speed 25ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Int / +1 Dex, −1 Str

Traits

  • Advantage on Will saves vs magic.
  • Chosen Expertise: Advantage on all checks with one chosen skill/craft, including building, repairing, or identifying small mechanical devices even outside that skill.
  • Advantage on Intelligence checks to solve a puzzle/riddle/mechanism under time pressure.
  • Advantage on checks to hide or squeeze through tight spaces despite encumbrance.
  • Clever Fallback: Once per day, reroll any one failed Intelligence check (1 Luck for a second use).
  • Weapon training: dagger, light hammer, hand crossbow, sling.

Subtypes

  • Tariel Gnome: Charisma-themed, Advantage on Charisma checks towards human communities, Advantage on trade/craft-commission/small-business checks.
  • Mournas Gnome: Constitution-themed, Advantage on saves vs frightened, Advantage on checks involving Mournas civic structure/remembrance/community organising.
  • Veradyna Gnome: Wisdom-themed, Advantage on Survival/Stealth within Veradyna's wilderness, Advantage on checks navigating/understanding Veradyna's native political landscape.

Goblin

Size Small • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Dex / +1 Con, −1 Wis

Traits

  • Mob Tactics: a creature with two or more of your allies adjacent to it can't make Attacks of Opportunity against you, and you can move through its space. Once per day, bonus damage = character level when damaging a larger creature (1 Luck for extra use).
  • Choose one skill at creation; you have Advantage on checks with it. This is not a Proficiency tier and is not one of your 3 starting skills.
  • Weapon training: shortsword, shortbow, sling, dagger.
  • Armour training: light.

Goliath

Size Large • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Str / +1 Con, −1 Int

Traits

  • Advantage on Strength checks to push, drag, lift or break against a smaller creature or object.
  • Resistance 5 to cold.
  • Mountain Endurance (Advantage on Fortitude saves against exhaustion, forced marching and thin mountain air). Once per day, when hit: reduce the damage by 1d12 + Constitution modifier (1 Luck for extra use).
  • Weapon training: two-handed axe, maul, javelin, greatclub.

Subtypes

  • Jotunas Goliath: Wisdom-themed, Advantage on Jotunas terrain/tribal-custom/true-giant-lineage checks, Advantage on Charisma checks towards Dul Khagul dwarves.
  • Tribe Greater Goliath (Strongroar Lands): Charisma-themed, Advantage on Strongroar Lands terrain/custom checks, Advantage on Charisma checks towards Tenor Hold dwarves.

Half-Elf

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Low-Light Vision (not true darkvision) • +2 Cha / +1 Dex, no penalty

Traits

  • Immune to magical sleep.
  • Advantage on saves vs charm.
  • Flexible Rest: fully rested from either a 4hr trance or 8hr sleep.
  • Choose one additional skill at creation; you have Advantage on checks with it. This is not a Proficiency tier and is not one of your 3 starting skills.
  • Advantage on social checks with both humans and elves.
  • Dual Heritage: Once per day, reroll any one failed save or check (1 Luck for a second use).
  • Weapon training: longsword, shortsword, longbow, plus one martial weapon of choice.
  • Armour training: light.

Half-Orc

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Str / +1 Con, −1 Cha

Traits

  • Relentless Endurance: 1/day, when damage of any kind would drop you to 0 HP or below, drop to 1 HP instead.
  • Choose one additional skill at creation; you have Advantage on checks with it. This is not a Proficiency tier and is not one of your 3 starting skills.
  • Brutal Strikes: on a critical hit, add one extra damage die of the weapon's type (passive, always on).
  • Onslaught: spend 1 Luck to make one additional weapon attack, as part of the same action, against a creature you've just damaged. It costs 1 Luck each time, with no daily limit.
  • Weapon training: two-handed axe, battleaxe, javelin, handaxe.
  • Armour training: light, medium.

Halfling

Size Small • Speed 25ft • Darkvision None • +2 Dex / +1 Cha, −1 Str

Traits

  • Lucky: on a natural 1 (attack, ability check, or save), reroll and must take the new result, up to 3 times per session. A Halfling who takes the Lucky feat has 4 in all.
  • Nimble: can move through the space of any larger creature.
  • Advantage on checks related to farming, foraging, or identifying plants.
  • Brave Heart: Advantage on saves against fear.
  • Weapon training: sling, shortsword, dagger, handaxe.

Hobgoblin

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Str / +1 Int, −1 Wis

Traits

  • Advantage on checks and saves to resist being frightened.
  • Advantage on Intelligence checks involving strategy, formation tactics, and reading a battlefield.
  • Fortune's Favour: once per day, out of turn, you or an ally within 30ft rerolls a missed attack roll or failed save (1 Luck for a second use).
  • Weapon training: longsword, longbow, glaive, light crossbow.
  • Armour training: light, medium.

Human

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision None • +1 / +1 to any two attributes of choice, no penalty

Traits

  • Choose one skill at creation; you have Advantage on checks with it. This is not a Proficiency tier and is not one of your 3 starting skills. It keeps its Advantage if you later train or master the skill.
  • Gains an additional Feat from the General Path (The Survivors) at 1st level, on top of their normal 1st-level Feat choice. It follows the usual prerequisites, and can't be a Feat you already have.
  • Weapon training: any two martial weapons of choice.
  • Armour training: light, medium.

Kobold

Size Small • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 90ft • +2 Dex / +1 Int, −1 Str

Traits

  • Pack Loyalty: Advantage on your first melee attack each round vs a creature an ally has damaged since your last turn.
  • Advantage on hide/squeeze/tactical-use-of-small-size checks.
  • Trapwise: Advantage on building/identifying/disarming/avoiding mechanical traps.
  • Disadvantage on attack rolls and sight-based Perception checks in direct sunlight.
  • Advantage on identifying dragon/dragon-kin lineage and on Charisma checks towards true dragons/other dragon-kin.

Subtypes

  • Deteron-born (currently bonded): Advantage on mining/tunnel-maintenance/serving-clan-customs checks; Advantage on saves vs compulsion or charm effects imposed by their own bonded dragon/clan (resisting the hand that holds the leash); Disadvantage on Charisma checks against their own bonded dragon/clan while in active service.
  • Komodo Isle (free-born or escaped): Advantage on Survival/navigation in jungle or island terrain; Advantage on saves vs charmed/dominated/compelled.

Lizardfolk

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Con / +1 Wis, −1 Int

Traits

  • Hold Breath up to 15 minutes. +1 natural armour AC. Advantage on Survival checks to track or forage in swamp/marsh/jungle terrain.
  • Bite unarmed strike: 1d4 + Strength modifier.
  • Swamp's Grip: Once per day, a successful bite also grapples the target, which must make a Fortitude save (Ancestry Save DC, Strength) or be restrained until the end of your next turn, no extra action required.
  • Advantage on Charisma checks towards other dragon-kin and true dragons.

Subtypes

  • East Deteron: Charisma-themed, Advantage on Aurethys customs/metallic-dragon-hierarchy checks, Advantage on saves vs fear.
  • West Deteron: Strength-themed, Advantage on saves vs charmed/dominated, Advantage on checks enduring/surviving harsh labour.
  • Komodo Isle: Dexterity-themed, Advantage on Survival/navigation in jungle/island terrain, Advantage on saves vs charmed/dominated/compelled.
  • Veradyna Marsh: Wisdom-themed, Advantage on Stealth/Survival specifically in marsh/wetland terrain, Advantage on checks involving Veradyna's native political landscape and tribal customs.

Mindryath

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Wis / +1 Cha, −1 Str

Traits

  • Advantage on saves vs charmed; immune to magical sleep.
  • Advantage on checks involving nature, plant growth, or communicating with fey/forest-dwelling creatures.
  • Roving Grace: Once per day, cross between the Feywild and the material plane without a portal or ritual, arriving at a place you have seen; you cannot bring passengers.
  • One Druid cantrip at creation.
  • Weapon training: staff, sickle, shortbow, dagger.

Minotaur

Size Large • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Str / +1 Con, −1 Int

Traits

  • Horns unarmed strike: 1d8 + Strength modifier.
  • Powerful Build (Advantage on Strength checks to push, drag or lift).
  • Labyrinthine Recall: never lost, always recalls a maze-like layout travelled once.
  • Horn Charge: an action. Move at least 10ft in a straight line, then make a Horns attack; on a hit it deals +1d6 damage.
  • Weapon training: battleaxe, two-handed axe, javelin, spear.

Subtypes

  • Red Waste/Veradyna: Wisdom-themed, Advantage on Survival in harsh/arid/wild terrain, Advantage on Intimidation checks.
  • Tenor Hold: Intelligence-themed, Advantage on Tenor Hold customs/craft/civic-life checks, Advantage on saves vs charmed/dominated specifically by fiendish/demonic influence.
  • Opal: Charisma-themed, Advantage on trade/negotiation/Opal-port-culture checks, Advantage on Charisma checks towards other integrating/non-native peoples in Opal.
  • Mournas: Advantage on saves vs frightened, Advantage on checks related to Mournas's civic structure/culture of remembrance, Advantage on Charisma checks towards Mournas's other freed populations.

Nu'Dravi (Drow)

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 120ft • +2 Dex / +1 Int, −1 Wis

Traits

  • Immune to magical sleep.
  • Advantage on saves vs charm.
  • Trance (4hr rest).
  • Advantage on Perception (sight/hearing) in low light or darkness.
  • Innate Dancing Lights at will; Darkness or Faerie Fire, 1/day (choose one when cast; Faerie Fire allows a Reflex save, Ancestry Save DC, Charisma).
  • Weapon training: hand crossbow, shortsword, rapier.
  • Armour training: light.
  • Sunlight Sensitivity varies by faith: Nu'Dravi who worship Eilistraee are exempt entirely.
  • Nu'Dravi of no faith or a neutral faith get a lesser version (Disadvantage only in the first hour of direct sunlight exposure per day).
  • Drow who worship Lolth keep full Sunlight Sensitivity (Disadvantage on attack rolls and sight-based Perception checks in direct sunlight).

Orc

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Str / +1 Con, −1 Int

Traits

  • Relentless Endurance: 1/day, when damage of any kind would drop you to 0 HP or below, drop to 1 HP instead.
  • When wielding a weapon two-handed, reroll any 1s on its damage dice once (keep the new result).
  • Advantage on Intimidation checks.
  • Orcish Charge: when you Charge and hit, the target is pushed 5ft.
  • Weapon training: two-handed axe, battleaxe, javelin, handaxe.
  • Armour training: light, medium.

Shifter

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Low-Light Vision (not true darkvision) • Constitution + lineage attribute (see below)

  • Canidae-Longtooth: +2 Con / +1 Str, −1 Int
  • Canidae-Wildhunt: +2 Con / +1 Wis, −1 Str
  • Felidae-Swiftstride: +2 Con / +1 Dex, −1 Wis
  • Ursidae-Beasthide: +2 Con / +1 Str, −1 Dex
  • Suidae-Gorebrute: +2 Con / +1 Str, −1 Cha
  • Ophidian: +2 Con / +1 Cha, −1 Int

Traits

  • The Beast Within (Shifting): once per encounter, shift as part of your action; the shift lasts the encounter.
  • Lineage benefits apply only while shifted.
  • Lineages: Canidae-Longtooth (Pack Attacker): Strength-themed; shifted: once per round, when you hit a creature an ally also threatens, it falls Prone if it is no larger than you (Fortitude save, Ancestry Save DC, Strength, negates).
  • Canidae-Wildhunt (Tracker): Wisdom-themed; shifted: Advantage on Perception/Survival involving scent or tracking.
  • Felidae-Swiftstride (Skirmisher, covers Catfolk): Dexterity-themed; shifted: +15ft speed.
  • Ursidae-Beasthide (Stoic Tank): Constitution-themed; shifted: Resistance 5 to nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing or slashing (choose one when you take this lineage), plus temporary HP equal to your Constitution modifier each time you shift.
  • Suidae-Gorebrute (Juggernaut/Disruptor): Strength-themed; shifted: may move through an enemy's space, forcing it to make a Fortitude save (Ancestry Save DC, Strength) or be knocked prone; once per creature per turn, and only creatures no more than one size larger.
  • Ophidian (Ambusher/Controller, yuan-ti blood): Charisma-themed; shifted: bite manifests venom (a successful unarmed bite forces a Fortitude save (Ancestry Save DC, Constitution) or the target is Poisoned; see Conditions in The Arneyan Codex).

Tiefling

"Tiefling" is what others call them. A tiefling is born into a family of another ancestry, human, orc, elf or any other, whose bloodline carries a fiendish curse. The mark can skip generations and appear in a child of ordinary-looking parents. There is no tiefling people, homeland or culture.

Size Medium • Speed 30ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Cha / +1 Int, −1 Wis

Traits

  • Family: choose the ancestry of the family you were born into. You speak its language, and others treat you as one of its people once they look past the marks. Your size, speed, vision and traits are the Tiefling's, whatever your family.
  • Resistance 5 to a damage type set by your bloodline.
  • One Warlock cantrip at creation.
  • Fiendish Retort: Once per day, when damaged by a creature within 30ft, unleash it back at them as part of your action on your next turn. The damage type is set by your bloodline: 1d6 at 1st, 1d8 at 5th, 2d6 at 9th, 2d8 at 13th, 3d6 at 17th.
  • From 11th level, Fiendish Retort can be used twice per day.

Bloodlines

  • Infernal (devils): horns, a tail, embers in the eyes. Resist fire; Retort deals fire. Advantage on checks to read, recall or find loopholes in contracts, oaths and bargains. You know Infernal.
  • Abyssal (demons): wild, twisted features that rarely look the same twice in a family. Resist poison; Retort deals acid. Advantage on Charisma checks to intimidate. You know Abyssal.
  • Outer (daemons, rakshasa and stranger fiends): subtle, unsettling marks that are hard to place. Resist necrotic; Retort deals necrotic. Advantage on checks to see through disguises and illusions. You know Infernal or Abyssal.
  • Shadowfell (fiends of shadow): ashen skin, a shadow that moves a moment late. Resist cold; Retort deals cold. Advantage on checks to hide in dim light or darkness. You know Infernal or Abyssal.

Ysoki

Size Small • Speed 25ft • Darkvision 60ft • +2 Dex / +1 Int, −1 Con

Traits

  • Advantage on Perception checks involving smell or hearing.
  • Cheek Pouch: stash small non-weapon items, retrieve without using an action.
  • Bite unarmed strike: 1d4 + Strength modifier.
  • Nimble Escape: when you Disengage you may also Hide, if cover is within reach.
  • Advantage on checks to navigate tunnels, sewers, and other confined underground spaces.
  • Weapon training: dagger, hand crossbow, sling, shortsword.

Each ancestry gives a fixed set: +2 to a primary attribute, +1 to a secondary one and, for most ancestries, −1 to a third. Humans instead take +1 to any two attributes of the player's choice, with no penalty.

  • Trade-off (optional rule): an ancestry with a penalty may drop the −1 by lowering its +2 to +1.
    • Choose once, at creation: the full bonus and the penalty, or the smaller bonus and no penalty.
    • It never applies to ancestries with no penalty (Human, Half-Elf).
    • It doesn't change if the GM later lets you retcon your ancestry mid-campaign.
  • Sub-types: use their parent ancestry's attribute bonuses and penalty. Regional and cultural variants (Gnome cultures, Elf cultures, Dwarf clans and so on) differ only in their traits and Advantages.
  • Shifter lineages and Genasi castes are the exception: each lineage or caste sets the ancestry's secondary attribute, so each has its own stat line, as Humans choose theirs.

This is a stats-only reference. For lore, origins and where each people lives (apart from the Tiefling's opening line), see the Arneyan setting material.

  • Sub-type entries: add to the ancestry's base traits rather than replacing them. A Dul Khagul Dwarf, for instance, has all of the base Dwarf's traits (stonework Advantage, poison Advantage and Resistance, chosen Craft skill, Clan Weapon) plus its own two Dul Khagul Advantages.

pages.name: How Attributes Work in This System

text.content:
There are six attributes (Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma), plus Luck as a separate seventh stat (see The Luck Stat). Each has a score, generated with Method V below, and the score gives a modifier that adds to the rolls it governs.

The Arneyan Modifier Table

Every attribute score converts to a modifier on this table. Monsters use the same table.

ScoreModifierScoreModifier
0Helpless or dead18+3
1–2−419–20+4
3−321–22+5
4–5−223–25+6
6–8−126–27+7
9–12+028–29+8
13–15+130+9
16–17+2

Rolled scores. Method V never produces a score above 18, and no score starts above 18 (see Starting Scores).

20 is the cap for mortals. Ancestry, feats and every other ordinary source can raise a score to 20 and no further. The only exception is a class's permanent attribute reward, which can carry a score to 22. Anything higher takes an extraordinary source such as legendary magic or a god's blessing; see The Mortal Limit. Scores above 22 belong to monsters, gods and legends.

What the Attributes Do

Strength: melee attack and damage, thrown and Strength-based weapons, carrying capacity (18 slots, 20 at Strength 13 to 15, 22 at 16+, 16 at 6 or less; see Inventory & Carrying Capacity in The Arneyan Codex), and feats of force.

Dexterity: Armour Class (within your armour's limit), initiative, ranged attack and damage, Finesse weapons, Reflex saves, and agility and stealth.

Constitution: Hit Points, Fortitude saves, endurance, and resisting poison and disease.

Intelligence: extra languages, lore, and the key attribute for Wizards, Illusionists, Necromancers, Spellblades and Artificers.

Wisdom: Will saves, awareness, insight and survival instincts, and the key attribute for Clerics, Druids and Witches.

Charisma: persuasion, deception, leadership, henchmen and hirelings, and the key attribute for Bards, Knights, Paladins, Sorcerers and Warlocks.

The Mortal Limit

The Cap. No attribute can exceed 20. Ancestry bonuses, Feat bonuses and every other ordinary source stop at 20, and any excess is lost. The one exception is the permanent attribute bonus a class grants as a level reward (such as +1 at 15th level): a class bonus can carry an attribute past 20, up to a maximum of 22.

Beyond Mortal Limits. Only extraordinary events lift a score past its cap.

  • Sources: legendary magic (a wish of the highest order, an ancient tome, an artefact), a god's blessing earned through deeds or devotion, or a bargain with a devil, a fey lord or another patron.
  • The price: the GM decides what is granted and sets the price. A blessing can be withdrawn if you break faith; a bargain is collected when it suits the other party.
  • On your sheet: note the source beside the score. If the source ends, so does the boost.
  • The modifier: the boost is added after the cap and uses the same modifier table, so a score of 23 gives +6. The table ends at 30, which no mortal reaches.

How Advantage Works

Advantage comes from GM discretion (situational), from Master training in an NWP (see Skills), from ancestry or class traits, manoeuvres and positioning (charging, flanking), and from other effects where listed. Roll two d20 and take the higher. Advantage and Disadvantage do not stack: any number of sources of one kind gives a single extra die, and one source of each cancels out so you roll one d20. Advantage never applies to damage rolls.

Ancestry Attribute Bonuses

Every ancestry grants a fixed attribute bonus/penalty pair: a +2 to a primary attribute, a +1 to a secondary attribute, and (for most ancestries) a −1 penalty to a third. Human instead gets +1/+1 to any two attributes of the player's choice, with no penalty. See Arneyan Ancestries for the full table.

Dice Set: six scores, one for each attribute. You roll two separate sets (Set Alpha and Set Beta) and keep one of them whole.

Method V

Roll six pools of d6s in this order. For each pool, add the three highest dice to get one score.

  • Pool 1: roll 8d6, keep the highest 3
  • Pool 2: roll 5d6, keep the highest 3
  • Pool 3: roll 4d6, keep the highest 3
  • Pools 4, 5 and 6: roll 3d6 each, keep all 3

The six scores are Set Alpha. Roll all six pools again to make Set Beta. Choose one set to keep and assign its six scores to your attributes however you wish. The set you do not keep may be donated to the table (Rule B).

Three table rules keep rolling fair and make sure no player is left with an unplayable hero.

Rule A: The Two-Set Choice (No Cherry-Picking)

You keep one entire set. You cannot swap individual scores between your two sets.

  • Illegal: Set Alpha is 18, 14, 13, 11, 10, 6 and Set Beta is 15, 14, 14, 12, 11, 10. You cannot take the 18 from Alpha and swap its 6 for a 10 from Beta.
  • Legal: take Set Alpha exactly as it is (the 18, but also the 6), or Set Beta exactly as it is (no 18, but no weakness).

Rule B: The Table Donation Rule

If you roll two good sets, keep your favourite and write the other on the whiteboard as a donation to the table. Any player whose own sets are poor can take a donated set instead of their own.

  • Example: Tamla rolls two good sets, keeps the better one for her Rogue and donates the other (16, 15, 14, 13, 11, 10). Alex rolls nothing above a 12, discards his own sets and builds his Paladin from Tamla's.

Rule C: The Gygaxian Threshold

A hero needs at least two scores of 14 or higher in the chosen set, before ancestry bonuses. If neither of your sets qualifies and no donated set is available, discard both and roll both sets again.

  • Example: Alex's Set Alpha is 13, 13, 12, 11, 9, 8 (no score of 14 or higher) and Set Beta is 14, 13, 11, 10, 10, 7 (only one). Both fail, so unless someone has donated a set, he rolls again.

Optional Rule: The Quick Roll

For a table that prefers a simpler roll, the GM may allow 4d6 instead of Method V. Roll 4d6 six times, dropping the lowest die each time, and assign the six results to your attributes as you like. Rule C still applies (two scores of 14 or higher, or roll again), and so does the starting cap of 18.

The starting cap. When a character is created, no score can go above 18, even after ancestry bonuses and feats. The cap applies at any starting level; attribute rewards from levels above 1st are added afterwards, and from then on scores follow The Mortal Limit.

Moving the excess. If your ancestry bonus, or an attribute bonus from a feat taken at creation (such as Steady Hand), would take a score above 18, put the points that would be lost into another attribute of your choice instead. That attribute also stops at 18.

Example 1: A Balanced Set

Alex rolls his pools in order: 8d6 (6,6,5,5,4,2,1,1 keeps 6,6,5 = 17); 5d6 (6,5,4,3,2 keeps 6,5,4 = 15); 4d6 (5,5,4,2 keeps 5,5,4 = 14); 3d6 (6,4,2 = 12); 3d6 (5,3,3 = 11); 3d6 (4,3,2 = 9). Set Alpha is 17, 15, 14, 12, 11, 9, which clears the Gygaxian Threshold. His Set Beta is 15, 13, 12, 11, 10, 8, so he keeps Set Alpha for a sharp-witted Wizard.

Example 2: A Big Score and a Big Flaw

Tamla's Set Alpha is 18, 16, 14, 11, 10, 4; her last 3d6 pool came up 2, 1, 1. She puts the 18 in Dexterity, the 16 in Intelligence and the 4 in Constitution: a brilliant marksman with a frail body. Her ancestry gives +2 Dexterity, which would take the 18 past the cap, so she moves both points to Intelligence instead (16 becomes 18).

Example 3: The Cursed Roller

Both of Alex's sets fail the Gygaxian Threshold (see Rule C). Tamla has a spare set (16, 15, 14, 13, 11, 10) and donates it, so Alex builds a strong frontline Paladin from it instead of rolling again.

The 8d6 pool averages about 15, the 5d6 about 13, the 4d6 about 12 and each 3d6 about 10½. About one set in five has a natural 18, so roughly one hero in three can choose a set with one, and about one player in seventeen fails the Gygaxian Threshold on both sets and needs a donated set or a fresh roll.
• Starting score: roll 4d6 and drop the lowest. This is your Starting Luck Score, set at character creation.

• Spend: each point of Luck spent adds +1 to a d20 roll (an attack roll, saving throw, ability or skill check; never damage).
  • When: declare it after you roll, but before the GM describes the outcome.
  • The cost: your Current Luck Score drops by the amount spent; your Starting Luck stays the same.

Sometimes the GM calls for a Luck Check to see whether fate is on your side ("Do you find a dry spot to camp?", "Does the monster target you?").

  • Succeeding: roll a d20 equal to or lower than your Current Luck Score. A natural 1 always succeeds and a natural 20 always fails, whatever your Luck.
  • The catch: the more Luck you burn for bonuses, the lower your chance on these checks.

When a character is reduced to 0 HP, they fall unconscious but stable; below 0 HP they begin dying (see Death & Dying in The Arneyan Codex). Luck can provide a narrow window of survival.

  • Last Chance: once each time they are dying, a dying character may burn 1 Luck to try to stabilise. Once they are stable, back at 0 HP or more, or dead, the next time they are dying brings a new chance.
  • The roll: a Fortitude save (DC 10). On a success the character stops dying and is stabilised, still unconscious at their current HP. On a failure they keep dying, and only an ally (Wisdom check, DC 10) or First Aid can stabilise them.
  • First Aid: the cantrip stabilises a dying creature without a roll.

Luck does not recover with sleep or rest. In the harsh world of Arneyan, you must earn your favour back.

  • Tenets: acting on one of your tenets when it costs you something may earn +1 Luck, at the GM's call (once per session at most).
  • Levelling up: each new level recovers 1 Luck.
  • Maximum: Luck can never exceed 20.
  • Feats: the Luck-raising feats (Fated Survivor, Lucky, Luck Battery, Skilled Regeneration) are exceptions to the recovery rules above.

Luck is a double-edged sword. A player who burns 5 points of Luck to land a killing blow on a boss might find themselves unable to pass a Luck check to avoid a pit trap ten minutes later. Remind your players: the more you lean on Fate, the faster she steps aside.

Every level costs 10 XP, for every class and for multiclass characters too (see How Levels Are Awarded in The Arneyan Codex). When your XP reaches 10, spend it to gain a level; anything left over carries towards the next, but one award never gives more than one level. You begin at 1st level, so 5th takes four fills (40 XP) and 20th takes nineteen.

Class GroupFeatsProgression Levels
Specialists: Assassins, Rogues, Swashbucklers71st, 3rd, 6th, 9th, 12th, 16th, 20th
Martials: Archers, Barbarians, Fighters, Gunslingers, Knights, Monks, Rangers61st, 3rd, 6th, 12th, 16th, 20th
Hybrids: Artificers, Paladins, Spellblades51st, 6th, 12th, 16th, 20th
Full casters: Bards, Clerics, Druids, Illusionists, Necromancers, Sorcerers, Warlocks, Witches, Wizards41st, 6th, 12th, 20th

Path Restrictions: Your class directly determines which specific Path table you can choose from.

Pure Classes: Must choose from their designated Path list or the General Path.

Two-Path Classes: Bards, Illusionists, Paladins, Rangers, Archers, Gunslingers, Swashbucklers, Rogues, Assassins, Monks, Artificers, and Spellblades may choose from either of their two Paths without multiclassing:

  • Bard: Specialist or Arcane & Devout
  • Illusionist: Specialist or Arcane & Devout
  • Paladin: Martial or Arcane & Devout
  • Ranger: Martial or Specialist
  • Archer: Martial or Specialist
  • Rogue: Martial or Specialist
  • Assassin: Martial or Specialist
  • Monk: Martial or Specialist
  • Gunslinger: Martial or Specialist
  • Swashbuckler: Martial or Specialist
  • Artificer: Specialist or Arcane & Devout
  • Spellblade: Martial or Arcane & Devout (a Shadow Edge Spellblade may also choose Specialist)

Multiclassing Access: The only way a pure class can gain access to multiple restricted Path tables. When you gain a Feat level, you may choose from the Path of any class you hold levels in.

Taking Feats: Each feat can be taken only once unless its entry says otherwise. A feat and a class feature of the same name do not stack; use the better.

Custom Feats: any character can work with the GM to design a custom feat that fits their character's story, abilities and class.

Attribute Bonuses: an attribute bonus from a Feat cannot take a score above 20, and bonuses from different Feats do not stack past that limit. See The Mortal Limit.

Raising an attribute: there is no plain attribute increase in place of a feat. Instead, nine General Path feats each give +1 to an attribute on top of their benefit: Toughness, Iron Constitution, Will of Iron, Steady Hand, Brute Force, Swift Reflexes, Keen Mind, Perceptive Grit and Charismatic Presence.

I. General Path (The Survivors)

Open to all classes by default.

Fated Survivor and Lucky (here), and Luck Battery and Skilled Regeneration (Specialist Path), are explicit exceptions to the normal Luck recovery rules; no other Feat changes how Luck is gained or recovered. Luck can never exceed 20.

Diehard When reduced to 0 HP or below, you can spend 2 points of Luck to instantly remain at 1 HP and stay conscious.

Fated Survivor Your Current Luck can never be burned below 1. Gain +1 to your Starting Luck Score immediately upon taking this Feat, with further +1 increases at each of 5th, 10th, 15th and 20th level reached after taking it (your Current Luck rises by the same amount, to a maximum of 20).

Inscrutable Fate When hit, you can spend 2 points of Luck to force a reroll (lower result used). Gain Advantage on Luck Checks against traps (roll twice and take the lower d20, since low is good on a Luck Check).

Lucky When you gain a level, recover 1d4+1 Luck instead of 1 (to a maximum of 20). If Luck Battery also applies, use the higher. Reroll one Natural 1, once per session (a Halfling adds this to the ancestry's 3, for 4 in all).

Battlefield Medic Treat wounds (Wisdom check, DC 15, Hard tier) to heal a target for HP equal to your Level + your Wisdom modifier (minimum +1). A healer can treat each target only once per day.

Quick Recovery At the start of your turn, you can spend 2 Luck to remove one condition (frightened, poisoned, prone, etc.) from yourself.

Toughness (Constitution) Gain +1 Max HP per level (retroactive). Gain +1 to Constitution (once, on taking this feat). Advantage on Constitution-based checks.

Iron Constitution (Constitution) Advantage on saving throws against poison and disease. Gain +1 to Constitution (once, on taking this feat).

Will of Iron (Wisdom, Intelligence or Charisma: choose one for the +1) Permanent +2 bonus to Will saving throws. Gain +1 to one of Wisdom, Intelligence, or Charisma of your choice (once, on taking this feat).

Steady Hand (Strength or Dexterity: choose one for the +1) Advantage on checks made to resist being disarmed, knocked prone, or moved against your will. Gain +1 to Strength or Dexterity of your choice (once, on taking this feat).

Brute Force (Strength) Advantage on Strength checks made to break, force open, or physically overpower an obstacle. Gain +1 to Strength (once, on taking this feat).

Swift Reflexes (Dexterity) Advantage on Initiative rolls. Gain +1 to Dexterity (once, on taking this feat).

Keen Mind (Intelligence) Advantage on Intelligence checks made to recall lore, history, or identify unfamiliar creatures and phenomena. Gain +1 to Intelligence (once, on taking this feat).

Perceptive Grit (Wisdom) Advantage on Perception checks made to avoid being surprised or ambushed. Gain +1 to Wisdom (once, on taking this feat).

Charismatic Presence (Charisma) Once per day, as part of your action, grant one ally within earshot Advantage on their next attack roll or ability check. Gain +1 to Charisma (once, on taking this feat).

Skilled You learn skills in half the time (see Learn New Skills in The Arneyan Codex), and gain one skill at Trained when you take this feat.

II. Martial Path

Available to: Fighters, Barbarians, Knights, Paladins, Spellblades, Bards, Rangers, Archers, Gunslingers, Swashbucklers, Rogues, Assassins, and Monks.

Armour Master: Gain +1 AC while wearing armour. You are trained in light armour (Padded Armour, Leather Armour and Studded Leather).

Intimidating Presence: Once per encounter, choose one enemy within 10ft. Unless it passes a Will save against your Class Save DC (using Charisma), it has Disadvantage for the rest of the round.

Cleave: You may use the Cleave manoeuvre up to twice per turn instead of once (three times a turn with a Cleaving weapon).

Combat Reflexes: Once per round, make an Attack of Opportunity (one melee attack) against an enemy you can see that leaves your melee reach or moves past or through it. Disengage prevents it.

Critical Strike: Your weapon attacks score a Critical Hit on a natural 20, or on a natural 19 that hits.

Flowing Strikes: Once per round, when you hit a creature with a melee attack, make one extra melee attack. Against the creature you just hit it is rolled with Disadvantage; against a different creature within your reach it is a normal roll. The extra attack cannot trigger Flowing Strikes again.

Grappler: You have Advantage on Grapple contests. A creature you grapple can't take the Disengage action, and you move at your full speed while dragging it.

Power Attack (Smash): With a Heavy melee weapon held in two hands, you may make an attack with Disadvantage. If it hits, roll one extra weapon damage die (two from 10th level).

Shield Bash: Once per round, when you hit a creature no more than one size larger than you with a melee attack while holding a shield, slam the shield in as part of the same attack. The target makes a Fortitude save against your Class Save DC, using Strength or Dexterity, whichever is higher, or is knocked Prone.

Shield Expert: +1 AC while wielding a shield, and add your shield's AC bonus to Reflex saves.

Shield Fighter: Use a shield as a second weapon without the normal two-weapon attack penalty. It is a Light weapon dealing 1d4 (1d6 for a Tower Shield), and it keeps its AC bonus.

Two-Weapon Fighting: Your off-hand attack no longer suffers Disadvantage. The same feat appears in the Specialist Path; you can only take it once.

Weapon Master: Choose one weapon type you are trained in. Once per round, reroll one missed attack roll with it, and gain +2 to Damage with it. You can take this feat again for a different weapon each time, never a weapon in the group a Fighter has specialised in. It can also be learned in downtime as a Trained Feat, with no check at the end (see Downtime: Training & Instruction in The Arneyan Codex).

Shove: Once per round, when you land a hit in melee on a creature no more than one size larger than you, you deal your damage and also shove the target 10ft away from you along the ground. Being shoved never provokes Attacks of Opportunity.

Felling Shot: Once per round, when you hit a creature no more than one size larger than you with a ranged weapon attack, it makes a Fortitude save against your Class Save DC, using Strength or Dexterity, whichever is higher, or is knocked Prone.

Covering Fire: Once per round, in place of one ranged attack, choose a creature you can see within your weapon's range. The next attack it makes before the start of your next turn has Disadvantage, unless it attacks you.

Practised Thrower: You draw a thrown weapon as part of the attack that throws it. Your thrown weapons' range and long range double, and after a fight you recover every thrown weapon that didn't break.

Point-Blank Terror: No Disadvantage for using ranged weapons within 5ft reach of an enemy. The same feat appears in the Specialist Path; you can only take it once.

Steady Aim: No Disadvantage on ranged attacks against a target engaged in melee with an ally. The same feat appears in the Specialist Path; you can only take it once.

III. Specialist Path

Available to: Rogues, Assassins, Rangers, Monks, Archers, Gunslingers, Swashbucklers, and Artificers.

Feint: Once per round, in place of one attack, make a Charisma (Deception) or Dexterity check against the target's Wisdom check. On a success, choose one: the target has Disadvantage on its next attack against you, or you have Advantage on your next attack against it.

Alertness: Cannot be surprised by nonmagical means; gain +2 to Initiative rolls. This stacks with Advantage on Initiative from other sources (such as Swift Reflexes or the Swashbuckler's En Garde).

Acrobatics: Halve falling damage; gain Advantage on checks to jump, climb, or manoeuvre. You can move through the spaces of enemies, and your movement never provokes Attacks of Opportunity.

Luck Battery: As part of your action, give up to 3 of your Current Luck points to an ally; they are not returned. Recover 2 Luck points instead of 1 upon levelling. If Lucky also applies, use the higher.

Master of Disguise: Advantage on checks to forge, impersonate, or maintain a disguise under scrutiny, and Advantage on the first Deception check made in any encounter. You can put together a convincing disguise in 1 minute, and once per day you may reroll a failed check to maintain a disguise or deception.

Mobile: Base movement increases by +10 feet.

Point-Blank Terror: No Disadvantage for using ranged weapons within 5ft reach of an enemy. The same feat appears in the Martial Path; you can only take it once.

Predator: Gain Advantage on Stealth checks. If you have Sneak Attack or Exploit, it deals +1d6.

Skilled Regeneration: When burning Luck turns a failed roll into a success, regain 1 of the Luck spent.

Two-Weapon Fighting: Your off-hand attack no longer suffers Disadvantage. The same feat as in the Martial Path; you can only take it once.

Steady Aim: No Disadvantage on ranged attacks against a target engaged in melee with an ally. The same feat appears in the Martial Path; you can only take it once.

Sure Footing: Ignore difficult terrain penalties to movement, and gain Advantage on checks to avoid or escape being restrained, grappled, or knocked prone.

Fate's Reversal: Spend 2 Luck to turn a natural 1 into a natural 20, on your own roll or an ally's within 30ft.

IV. Arcane & Devout Path

Available to: Wizards, Clerics, Druids, Illusionists, Paladins, Spellblades, Bards, Sorcerers, Warlocks, Witches, Necromancers, and Artificers.

Blood Magic: Cast a spell when you are out of slots by taking 1d6 damage per spell level. You can only do this while your current HP is higher than the most it could cost (6 per spell level). The HP cost is the only limit. It cannot be used to cast healing spells, and the damage cannot be healed by magic until the next day. The cost can't be reduced, resisted or soaked by temporary HP: it comes straight off your HP.

Ritual Caster: Any spell of 3rd level or lower that you know, other than a healing spell, and that doesn't require an instantaneous action in combat, can be cast as a 10-minute ritual instead of spending a slot, provided you're not under threat of imminent combat. Each spell can be ritual-cast once per day. Sorcerers cannot take this feat.

Steady Focus: You have Advantage on saves made to keep a spell you are casting, or to maintain concentration on one, when you take damage, are shoved or are otherwise forced to react mid-cast, and you can't lose a spell to damage of 5 or less.

Healer: Healing spells and brewed potions restore an additional +1 HP per die, and once per day you may cast a healing spell of 3rd level or lower without expending a slot.

Expanded Mind: You gain one additional spell slot of your highest currently available spell level.

Potent Casting: Your spells ignore damage resistance (but not immunity).

Signature Spell: Choose one spell of 3rd level or lower that you can cast. Once per day, you can cast it without expending a slot.

Familiar Bond: A small creature has bound itself to you: a bat, cat, owl, rat, raven, toad or weasel. It works as the familiar from the Summon Familiar spell, without casting it. You share its senses within 100ft without concentrating, and it can deliver your touch spells. If it dies, another finds you after 1 week. Witches can't take this feat; they already have a familiar.

War Caster: You have Advantage on Fortitude saves made to keep a spell you are casting, or to maintain concentration on one, when you take damage. You can perform the somatic components of spells while holding weapons or a shield in one or both hands. Choose one type of Light or Medium armour, or a shield: you are trained in it, so wearing it does not block your casting. (If your class is already trained in it, this last benefit adds nothing.)

Cantrip Mastery: Learn two additional cantrips from your class spell list. Once per round, when you cast a cantrip, add your casting-stat modifier (minimum +1) to its damage or healing when it hits or the target fails its save. It does not stack with Agonising Blast, and it adds to only one of Eldritch Blast's two blasts.

Arcane Insight: Once per day, cast any divination-type spell you know as a ritual investigation over 10 minutes without expending a slot, usable outside combat. You also have Advantage on Intelligence checks to identify spells, magic items and magical effects.
Skills (non-weapon proficiencies, NWPs) are trades, lore and specialist know-how for use outside combat.

Starting Skills. Every character starts Trained in 3 different skills, and none at Master. More are learned in downtime, with no limit and no link to level (see Learn New Skills under Downtime Rules in The Arneyan Codex).

Training Tiers. NWP training works in three tiers.

  • Untrained: a plain d20 with no attribute modifier. A specialised task isn't forbidden without the NWP; you simply roll untrained.
  • Trained: d20 + the modifier of the skill's attribute. If that modifier is 0 or less, add +1 instead.
  • Master: as Trained, with Advantage. A Master of a crafting skill also pays a third of an item's market price instead of half when crafting it (see Downtime: Crafting in The Arneyan Codex).

Reaching Master. A Trained skill becomes Master through more downtime with a teacher who is a Master of it: your modifier plus Advantage on checks with it.

Standardisation. There is no class restriction on skills: any character can learn any NWP regardless of class.

Everyday Checks. Ordinary actions are plain attribute checks and need no NWP.

  • Which actions: sneaking, noticing things, easy climbing (a ladder, a tree, a low wall), reading a person, intimidating or deceiving someone.
  • Names in rules: Stealth, Perception or Insight in a trait, feature or feat are shorthand for that kind of check: Dexterity to sneak, Wisdom to notice or read a person, Charisma to intimidate or deceive.
  • Persuasion: persuading an NPC is mostly roleplay. The GM calls for a Charisma check only when the outcome is truly in doubt.
  • NWPs cover trades, lore and specialist skills. Rolled untrained, they are a plain d20 with no modifier.
  • Ancestry skills: a skill an ancestry lets you choose can be an NWP or a kind of everyday check.

Thief Skills. Lockpicking, Traps, Pick Pocket and Climb use the tiers above, with these differences.

  • Lockpicking (Dexterity, with thieves' tools): Untrained, only an Easy or Moderate lock (DC 12 or less); Trained, any lock. Each character gets one attempt per lock until they gain a level.
  • Traps (Intelligence): Untrained, mechanical traps only, with Disadvantage; Trained, any mechanical trap; Master also covers magical traps (see Traps in The Arneyan Codex).
  • Pick Pocket (Dexterity): DC 10 + the target's Level. Untrained, with Disadvantage.
  • Climb (Strength; a Rogue or Assassin rolls Dexterity): walls, cliffs and mountains. Trained or Master, you climb at normal speed.
  • Rogues are Trained in all four from 1st level and Master from 5th, and have better versions of each (see the Rogue).

Tools. Crafting and trade skills need the matching toolkit (see the Toolkits table). With no usable tools you cannot craft; with improvised tools the roll has Disadvantage.

• Outlook: every character has one. Pick the combination (Law, Neutrality or Chaos with Good, Neutrality or Evil) that best fits how your character behaves, plus one or two tenets in your own words, such as "Never leave a companion behind". Outlook guides roleplay; the GM doesn't police it.
  • Allegiance: a true place in the cosmic war. Gods, fiends, celestials and the undead have one by nature; a mortal is Unaligned unless they take a side. True Neutral as an Allegiance is a sworn stance of balance.
  • Not a restriction: no class, Kit, Feat Path or multiclass combination requires or forbids any Outlook or Allegiance.

Divine service: a Cleric, Paladin or Battle Priest holds their god's alignment as their Allegiance while their god favours them (see Divine Favour).

Pacts: a Warlock holds their patron's alignment. A pact with a fiend makes you Evil, whatever your Outlook.

Profane acts: animating the dead, summoning or bargaining with fiends, enslaving people and murder pull a mortal towards Evil; repeated or sustained acts, such as keeping undead raised, make them Evil. Killing in battle or self-defence isn't murder; loosing a summoned evil creature is profane. For a god's servant, one is a flagrant breach unless the god's tenets allow it; they keep the god's Allegiance while favoured.

An Allegiance from service or a pact ends with it; one from profane acts ends with atonement.

Societies: cultures lean towards the powers behind them, such as a warband raised under an evil war god. A leaning shapes a people's laws and customs, but each of them keeps free will. The World of Arneyan wiki gives each culture's leaning.

Clerics, Paladins and Battle Priests serve a god with tenets, listed on that god's page in the World of Arneyan wiki. A Paladin's oath is their god's tenets plus one personal vow, chosen at 1st level.

  • Favoured: the normal state.
  • Strained: after a flagrant breach of the god's tenets or the Paladin's oath. Turn Undead and your highest-level spells need a DC 12 check with your key attribute (Wisdom, or Charisma for Paladins) as you use them; a failure spends the use or slot.
  • Forsaken: after a second flagrant breach while Strained, or on abandoning the god. You lose every class ability your god grants, Divine Mount included, until you atone; the rest stay.

Atonement (a quest, an offering or the Atonement spell, as the GM sets) moves you one step back towards Favoured.

Spells, items and features: anything that names an alignment ("evil creatures", Detect Alignment, holy water, Holy Word) affects only creatures with that Allegiance. Unaligned mortals don't register, whatever their Outlook.

Outsiders: celestials and fiends react to a character's Allegiance and perceived Outlook, as the GM decides.

Luck: the GM may award +1 Luck, once per session, when a character acts on a tenet at real cost.

Curses and possession: an effect that changes a character's alignment changes their Outlook. The player takes a fitting flaw, and may earn +1 Luck for playing it at a cost; it never costs XP.

Inventory is tracked in slots, not weight. Check what you can carry before you buy.

Base capacity: 18 slots, adjusted by Strength: 22 slots at Strength 16+, 20 at 13 to 15, 18 at 7 to 12 (the baseline) and 16 at 6 or less.

  • Standard gear: 1 slot
  • Heavy or two-handed items: 2-3 slots
  • Ammunition: 30 per slot
  • Coins: 100 per slot
  • Minor/light items (ink, quills, wax, scrolls, gems of the same tier): bundle up to 5 per slot
  • A Backpack provides the grid itself, takes no slot, and is usually the first thing anyone buys
  • Worn and Wielded: armour you wear, shields and weapons you carry all count against your slots.
  • Over the Limit: while you carry more than your capacity, your speed drops 10ft at 1 to 4 slots over, 20ft at 5 to 9 over, and a further 10ft for every 5 slots beyond that, to a minimum of 0, applied after anything that halves speed. You also have Disadvantage on Dexterity checks and attack rolls.

  • A level in another class adds none. To gain more, train in downtime with a teacher, and pay (see Downtime: Training & Instruction in The Arneyan Codex).
  • Class penalties still apply: a Rogue in heavy armour still loses the Rogue abilities that need light or no armour.
  • A class that lists "None" for armour still can't cast in it (see Spellcasting in Arneyan, VI).

Advancement: your XP is one shared pool, and every level costs 10 XP, as for any character (see How Levels Are Awarded in The Arneyan Codex). More classes cost nothing extra.

  • Spend 10 XP to gain one level in any of your classes, or in a new one with the GM's approval. Anything left over carries towards the next.
  • Your Character Level is your total levels across all classes.
  • Example: a Rogue / Wizard pays 10 XP for every level, whichever class it goes into.

Class Level: Each class has its own Class Level. Class abilities, spell slots, caster level and other class features use that class's Class Level. Hit Points, saving throws (half your level (minimum 1)), and Feat levels use Character Level.

Spellcasting: Each spellcasting class keeps its own spell slots, spell list, casting stat and spell DC (10 + half your caster level (minimum 1) + that class's casting-stat modifier, with caster level equal to that class's Class Level). Bonus slots from a high casting stat apply to each casting class's own table. Cantrips scale with the caster level of the class that casts them.

When you gain a Feat level, you may choose from the Path of any class you hold levels in. A Fighter/Cleric multiclass can pick from Martial Path or Arcane & Devout Path at any Feat level, regardless of which class's level triggered it. Feat levels follow the Feat Progression table for your first class.

If any of your classes has Kits or Paths, choose one for it when you first gain a level in it (your first at creation). They never share or double up, and their level-based features use that class's Class Level.
